title: Quantum computing with QuantLearn
audience: Beginners with basic algebra. Worked refreshers explain complex magnitudes, normalization, matrix action, tensor products and expectations. Advanced chapters introduce small examples, not expert-level mastery.

chapterQuiz.scoring: One point per correct answer; no negative marking; show explanations after submission; unlimited retries.
chapterQuiz.completion: Read the lesson and submit the chapter quiz. Record the score separately; quiz length follows the chapter and there is no pass threshold or prerequisite lock.
chapterQuiz.difficultyPolicy: Each quiz includes easy, medium and hard questions; the chapter determines the total.

basisConvention: q0 is the top circuit wire and least significant bit. Display bitstrings and statevector entries as |q(n-1)...q0>. Cirq examples explicitly reverse qubit_order and measurement order to match; PennyLane integer wires are normalized to the same display order.

modules.title: Quantum Foundations
modules.description: Understand states, phase and measurement before building your first circuit.

modules.title: Gates and Circuits
modules.description: Learn how gates transform states and how to read multi-qubit circuits.

modules.title: Entanglement and Communication
modules.description: Explore shared quantum states and the teleportation protocol.

modules.title: Quantum Algorithms
modules.description: Follow small, worked examples of quantum search and optimization.

modules.title: Simulation and Frameworks
modules.description: Read simulation results and compare the same experiment in Aer, Cirq and PennyLane.

chapters.summary: Separate bits, probabilities, amplitudes and the limits of one measurement.
chapters.title: Classical and quantum information
objectives: Distinguish a classical bit, a probability distribution and a qubit state.
Explain why a qubit is not simply a hidden pair of classical bits.
Describe what one measurement can and cannot reveal.

chapters.summary: Build the small mathematical toolkit needed to read quantum states and gates.
chapters.title: The mathematics toolkit
objectives: Use complex magnitudes and squared magnitudes as probabilities.
Normalize a statevector and explain why its norm matters.
Read a matrix as a transformation of a vector.

chapters.summary: Read state notation and turn complex amplitudes into probabilities.
chapters.title: Quantum bits and state notation
objectives: Read a two-entry statevector.
Convert amplitudes into probabilities.
Distinguish a qubit state from a classical probability list.

chapters.summary: See how relative phase changes interference and measurement outcomes.
chapters.title: Superposition, phase and interference
objectives: Distinguish global and relative phase.
Explain interference using two paths.
Predict HH and HZH outputs.

chapters.summary: Distinguish a single outcome, repeated shots and measurement bases.
chapters.title: Measurement and repeated shots
objectives: Apply the Born rule.
Separate probabilities from finite counts.
Explain measurement in Z and X bases.

chapters.summary: Read a circuit as time, transformations, measurements and classical outputs.
chapters.title: The quantum circuit model
objectives: Read wires, gates, time steps and measurement outputs.
Distinguish reversible unitary operations from measurement.
Translate a short circuit between diagram and matrix order.

chapters.summary: Apply the basic gates and work out why their order matters.
chapters.title: Single-qubit gates
objectives: Use I, X, Y, Z and H.
Multiply a gate by a statevector.
Explain why gate order matters.

chapters.summary: Connect phase shifts and rotation angles to measurable probabilities.
chapters.title: Phase and rotation gates
objectives: Compare S, T, Rx, Ry and Rz.
Interpret rotation angles in radians.
Relate rotations to the Bloch sphere.

chapters.summary: Build product states, expand tensor products and count amplitudes as registers grow.
chapters.title: Multi-qubit states and tensor products
objectives: Form tensor-product states.
Calculate basis amplitudes and probabilities by hand.
Explain why n qubits require 2^n amplitudes.

chapters.summary: Use controlled gates, measure circuit resources and debug bit-order conventions.
chapters.title: Controlled gates, circuit resources and bit ordering
objectives: Read CX, CZ and SWAP control and target semantics.
Separate gate count, circuit depth and hardware connectivity.
Debug Qiskit, Cirq and QuantLearn bit-order conventions.

chapters.summary: Move from pure statevectors to mixed states, reduced states and local Bloch vectors.
chapters.title: Density matrices and reduced states
objectives: Construct a density matrix for a pure state and a classical mixture.
Read diagonal probabilities and off-diagonal coherence.
Use a partial trace to explain why local state information can hide joint correlations.

chapters.summary: Select Bell states, compare Z and X correlations and separate coherence from ordinary correlation.
chapters.title: Bell states and correlations
objectives: Name and prepare the four Bell states.
Compare Z-basis and X-basis correlations with a classical mixture.
Explain why the shown comparison is not a universal Bell test.

chapters.summary: Trace how entanglement and two classical bits transfer a quantum state.
chapters.title: Teleportation and classical control
objectives: Follow a three-qubit teleportation circuit.
Select corrections from two classical bits.
Explain why teleportation neither clones nor sends information faster than light.

chapters.summary: Use linearity and reduced states to see what entanglement cannot clone, signal or reveal early.
chapters.title: No-cloning, no-signalling and limits of entanglement
objectives: Explain the no-cloning theorem with linearity and inner products.
Show why teleportation consumes the input and needs classical communication.
Distinguish correlation from a controllable faster-than-light message.

chapters.summary: Use phase kickback to distinguish constant and balanced functions.
chapters.title: Deutsch-Jozsa and phase kickback
objectives: State the constant-or-balanced promise.
Trace a two-input XOR oracle.
Interpret query complexity without overstating practical advantage.

chapters.summary: Follow a phase oracle and diffusion step to amplify a marked answer.
chapters.title: Grover search and amplitude amplification
objectives: Distinguish an oracle from measurement.
Calculate one diffusion step.
Explain the stopping rule and oracle-cost caveat.

chapters.summary: Encode a small max-cut problem and trace a cost and mixer layer.
chapters.title: QAOA and combinatorial optimization
objectives: Encode a one-edge max-cut objective.
Trace a p=1 cost/mixer circuit.
Explain parameter search and absence of guaranteed practical advantage.

chapters.summary: Estimate an energy and check a variational ansatz against an exact minimum.
chapters.title: VQE and energy estimation
objectives: Define an ansatz and Hamiltonian.
Estimate energy from Pauli expectation values.
Check an analytic minimum against a variational curve.

chapters.summary: Compare representations, sampling uncertainty and physical noise.
chapters.title: Simulation, noise and result displays
objectives: Compare statevector, density matrix and sampling.
Distinguish noise from shot uncertainty.
Read Bloch, statevector, histogram and circuit panels.

chapters.summary: Read equivalent Python circuits and align their output conventions.
chapters.title: The same circuit in Qiskit Aer, Cirq and PennyLane
objectives: Read all three Python APIs.
Normalize basis ordering.
Choose between sampled results and exact-state inspection.
